Theme

Nature & food

oak noun

also oaken, oak (adjective), oak wood

classical

Traupman 352

quercus, quercūs f.

noun, fourth declension

Tree names are mostly feminine, even in the second declension; rubus is masculine.

Other words

  • rōbur, rōboris n. — hard oak, oak-wood; an oak tree

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 3.13: nāvēs tōtae factae ex rōbore (Lewis & Short); Traupman 352

  • rōboreus, rōborea, rōboreum — oaken, made of oak

    declension · also used · classical · Ov. F. 5.622: pōns (Lewis & Short); Traupman 352

Examples

  • quercūs, tiliae, fraxinī, salicēs rīvō imminentēs, jūglandēs, corylī, cornī

    oaks, limes, ashes, willows overhanging the stream, walnuts, hazels, cornelian cherriescomposed

  • Duae arborēs ibi stant etiam nunc, quercus et tilia, truncīs vīcīnīs, rāmīs jūnctīs.

    Two trees stand there even now, an oak and a lime, their trunks side by side, their branches joined (Baucis and Philemon).composed

See also lime, beech, forest.

SourcesLewis & Short: quercus · Lewis & Short: robur · Lewis & Short: roboreus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 352.
